section_summary.extract_value: This Discussion section presents findings from a study examining how body image dimensions (body appreciation and appearance dissatisfaction) predict sexual health indicators in adult women of various ages. The study found that body appreciation was a unique predictor of better sexual function, satisfaction, and decreased distress, independent of BMI and appearance dissatisfaction. Notably, body appreciation did not vary significantly by age, suggesting it remains stable across the lifespan, and it moderated the relationship between age and sexual satisfaction, particularly for women with sexual function difficulties.
section_summary.evidence_source: The entire Discussion section describes the study's findings and implications regarding body appreciation, appearance dissatisfaction, age, and sexual health outcomes in women.

section_summary.extract_value: This Discussion section presents findings from a single study examining how body image (both positive and negative aspects) predicts sexual health indicators in adult women of various ages. The study found that body appreciation was a unique predictor of better sexual function, increased satisfaction, and decreased distress, and importantly, body appreciation moderated the relationship between age and sexual satisfaction in women with clinically significant sexual difficulties (FSD), as illustrated in Figure 1 which shows BAS moderation effects on the relationship between age and sexual satisfaction across FSD and no-FSD groups.

Asset Caption.extract_value: Fig. 1 Moderation effect of body appreciation on the relationship between age and sexual satisfaction in women with and without clinically significant sexual difficulties. FSD refers to significant sexual difficulties (FSFI < 26.55), whereas no FSD refers to no significant sexual difficulties (FSFI > 26.55)
